articles.title: Overcoming Cloudflare Blocks on Preply to Analyze Tutor Pricing Trends
articles.summary:

articles.title: Andrew Kelley Interview: Why He Built Zig, Banned AI Contributions, and Moved Zig off GitHub
articles.summary: In a JetBrains interview, Zig creator Andrew Kelley expanded on the project’s formal ban on AI contributions and the motivation behind its migration off GitHub to Codeberg: automated code submissions decrease codebase quality and weaken the social constructs between open-source participants; persistent GitHub failures and a perceived misalignment of incentives led to migrating to Codeberg. By Bruno Couriol

articles.title: AI-Powered Performance Testing Platform for Modern Engineering Teams
articles.summary:
Performance testing often takes a lot of time because teams have to create scripts, run tests, and fix them whenever something changes.

PeakoQ is an AI-powered performance testing platform that makes this process easier. You can import API collections from Postman, Swagger, or cURL and generate performance test scripts for JMeter and K6 without extensive scripting.

When a test fails, the Auto Healer helps identify the issue and automatically updates the script.

PeakoQ helps QA and engineering teams reduce manual effort and continuously test application performance before production.

articles.title: Changesets v3: Bumps Peer Dependents by Patch and Ships ESM Only with an 88% Smaller Install
articles.summary: Changesets v3.0, released on August 11, 2026, introduces significant updates for JavaScript monorepos. It offers leaner installations, a rebuilt CLI, and changes to peer dependency management that resolve long-standing complaints. Upgrading involves configuration updates. The tool focuses on versioning and changelogs while supporting contributors in declaring release intents. By Daniel Curtis

articles.title: Simulating fault tolerance with stage skipping in pipeline-parallel training [R]
articles.summary: Our most recent work at Templar explores fault tolerance in Crucible, our distributed pre-training platform. The goal is to keep healthy workers training when another pipeline stage goes offline. Crucible combines data-parallel replicas with pipeline parallelism. Each replica holds a copy of the model, split into stages on separate workers.
